description: Sad-girl moments — in scene (me & my friends)
llm_system_prompt: You invent SAD GIRL moments — hyper-specific situationship/emotional scenarios — that fit metaphor patterns derived from a meme image, and you map each moment's elements with honest scores. You only respond in JSON.
llm_user_prompt:
Plain visual read of the image (pixels only — the ground truth for what the scene visibly shows):
${step1Output}

Metaphor situations (abstract patterns this image could stand for):
${step4Output}

The image's physical analog (core = the binding relational skeleton; secondary = nice-to-have texture that never gates):
${step2Output}

THIS REGISTER'S READ (the in-scene ensemble — who each figure is):
${step5Output}

THE PERSONA (every moment comes from her world):
A sad girl — very funny, very self-aware, probably in a toxic situationship. Her world: situationships, avoidant men, rereading texts, going back after saying she's done, telling her friends everything, fake "i don't care" energy, trying not to crash out.

WRITE 1-3 sad girl moments (in THIS step's register) that could plausibly fit one of the metaphor situations AND whose entities can fill the analog CORE's slots with matching kind and cardinality. A moment that matches a situation's theme but cannot fill the core's slots does not qualify. Secondary texture never gates.

Every moment is ONE sentence in plain sad-girl register and MUST:
- contain ONE exact filmable behavior, never a vague word (WRONG: "overthinking his message" / RIGHT: "rereading his 'lol' six times after opening up to him" — illustrations only, never copy into output)
- name its entities concretely (me, my situationship, my friends, the group chat, his ex, Hinge) — entities that can FEEL or PROJECT an emotion
- use a DIFFERENT trigger from the other moments, not rewordings of one
- STAND ALONE — BE EXPLICIT: from the sentence ALONE a reader can tell WHO each entity is to her, WHAT just happened (the trigger event, spelled out in the sentence), and WHAT she is visibly doing about it. No unexplained reactions: if the moment shows a response (blocking, crying, celebrating), the thing being responded to is IN the sentence.
WRONG: "Smiling 'i feel so free' as my friends block him on every app" — blocking him WHY? the trigger never appears
RIGHT: "Smiling 'i feel so free' while my friends block him on every app after his third 3am 'you up?' this week — his number still on a napkin in my pocket"
(Illustrations only — never copy them into output.)

MATCH THE STAKES: an extreme visible reaction in the image demands a high-stakes trigger (he soft launches another girl while still texting you good morning); a mundane scene demands a mundane behavior.

THE READ IS THE CAST: every moment is told with THIS register read's ensemble — each figure keeps the entity the read assigned it (state-stamped or tightly varied forms welcome; a different identity is not). A moment that cannot be told with the read's ensemble does not qualify.
WRONG: two men celebrating ← a moment cast as "me and my best friend" — the poster test fails
RIGHT: the same figures ← "my delusion and my urge to text him hyping each other up" — forces fit any figure
(Illustrations only — never copy them into output.)

THIS STEP'S REGISTER: in_scene — she (or her friends) IS a figure in the scene. Every moment's entities land on the figures exactly as the in-scene read casts them.

For EACH moment:
1. "context": the moment — ONE sentence, sad-girl register, containing its exact behavior AND its spelled-out trigger. Its "register" is always "in_scene" in this step.
2. "metaphor": the metaphor situation it fits, copied VERBATIM from the list above.
3. "element_map": break that metaphor situation into its ELEMENTS — the actors, forces, and relations that make the pattern what it is (for a pattern like "ignoring an obvious problem while carrying on as normal": the obvious problem, the people carrying on, the normalcy being kept up). For each element, name who or what in the moment plays it, with a score 0-1 and a one-sentence reason. An element must be something that can FEEL or PROJECT an emotion, or a nameable force — NEVER a bare event or activity. An element nothing in the moment plays gets played_by null and score 0.0. CARDINALITY CAPS THE SCORE (mechanical): a plural or collective element (a team, a group, several X) played by a singular entity — or the reverse — scores 0.4 or below, no exceptions.
4. "core_fit": how well the moment's entities fill the analog CORE's slots — matching kind and cardinality. One-sentence reason naming who or what fills each slot. Secondary texture never raises or lowers this.
5. "overall": the overall fit 0-1 — never higher than the weakest element's score or core_fit; the reason names the weakest aspect.

Output the moments best overall first.

Output ONLY strict JSON (placeholders are NOT values; never copy them):
{
  "matches": [
    {
      "context": "<the moment — ONE sentence, sad-girl register, containing its exact behavior AND its spelled-out trigger>",
      "register": "in_scene",
      "metaphor": "<the metaphor situation, copied VERBATIM from the list>",
      "element_map": [
        { "element": "<one element of the metaphor pattern>", "played_by": "<who or what in the moment plays it, or null>", "score": <0-1>, "reason": "<one sentence>" }
      ],
      "core_fit": { "score": <0-1>, "reason": "<one sentence: who or what fills each core slot>" },
      "overall": { "score": <0-1>, "reason": "<one sentence naming the weakest aspect>" }
    }
  ]
}
